words.gloss: him who speaks useless words repeatedly

literal: Calling him who speaks words without usefulness a man is calling him the chaff of humanity.
translation: To call a person who repeatedly utters useless words a human being is like calling empty chaff a grain.
modern: பயனற்ற சொற்களைப் பேசித் திரிகிறவனை மனிதன் என்று சொல்லக் கூடாது; அவனை மனிதர்களுள் பதர் (பயனற்ற உமி) என்றுதான் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful agricultural metaphor to describe someone who speaks useless words. Just as chaff (பதடி) looks like grain from the outside but contains no substance inside, a person who speaks without purpose or utility may look like a human being (மகன்) but lacks any real human worth. The word 'பாராட்டுவான்' here refers to one who repeatedly utters or dwells on useless talk. The author emphasizes that such a person should not be counted among true human beings, but rather dismissed as empty chaff.
